correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern unnamed opening and north-to-northwest headward branch
correspondence.finding: The complete upper original depicts the chosen opening on an unnamed Quebrada-type feature and its northwestern continuation to the northward trunk. The source exposes the Arco del Choapa and Agua Fria tributary joins, the intervening unnamed northward course, the northwest bend, and the join to Estero De Ortega. All four selected opening parts follow this ordinary channel-and-join sequence. Their source NOMBRE fields are blank; neither nearby tributary name is extended over the chosen branch. The small selected/source offsets do not change the mapped branch sequence and are not subjected to a bank- or vertex-level test.

correspondence.component_scope: Estero de Ortega receiving reach
correspondence.finding: The selected route joins the directly named Estero De Ortega and follows its northward continuation to the Chicharra junction. The selected eastern headward branch is separate from the longer named Ortega branch arriving from the southwest. IGM publishes E. de Ortega on this receiving reach; the abbreviation is retained as a source form, not a registry decision.

correspondence.component_scope: Río de la Chicharra from the Ortega junction to Choapa
correspondence.finding: MMA directly labels the joined northwestward then northward river Río De La Chicharra and exposes its complete confluence with the east-arriving Choapa. IGM directly labels the same returned reach Rio de La Chicharra. The eastern Chicharra headbranch is not part of the chosen selection. The adjacent Río Del Valle is a different western tributary and is not the selected upper course.

correspondence.component_scope: Choapa receiving junction, western bend and northwestern upper trunk
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the source-named Choapa at the Chicharra junction, turns west, receives the separate Río Del Valle corridor, and continues north then northwest. The successful upper original supplies all selected intervening parts and joins. The Choapa name applies to this receiving trunk, while Chicharra and the unnamed headward drainage remain distinct components.

correspondence.component_scope: Choapa through the Cuncumén, Manque, Quelen and Chalinga junction sequence
correspondence.finding: The overlapping complete upper and middle originals expose the westward course below Cuncumén/Tencadan, the Manque join, the northwestward Quelen junction reach, and the Chalinga receiving junction. Every selected part in this interval is exposed and follows the Choapa trunk at ordinary corridor scale. Neighboring tributary names are not adopted as whole-system aliases. No selected lake, reservoir or managed-transfer interruption is depicted in this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Choapa past Camisas and Limahuida to the Illapel junction
correspondence.finding: The complete lower original maps the selected downstream continuation past the separate Camisas and Limahuida tributaries, through the intervening bends to the Illapel junction. The direct channel attributes consistently use Río Choapa. The Illapel watercourse joins from the northeast and retains its distinct tributary identity. Local alternate strands around short lower bends do not introduce a different basin or unestablished selected through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Choapa below Illapel, Canela junction, coastal turn and actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: The MMA hydrographic original directly names the receiving trunk Río Choapa below the distinct Río Illapel junction, around the western coastal turn, and into the terminal lagoon/wetland setting beside the Millahue join. The complete wetland original depicts the receiving riverine polygon and connected coastal lagoon polygons through the actual selected ending. Thus the final selected southwestward reach and endpoint have ordinary channel-to-waterbody correspondence; an additional offshore extension or present-day open sea outlet is not inferred. No meaningful through-link remains missing.
correspondence.source_specific_name_caution: Relevant coastal wetland inventory polygons use Rio Illapel. This source-specific label is preserved without renaming the directly labelled Choapa channel, claiming a formal alias or imposing one name on the coastal waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening in the Cerro Corá setting
correspondence.finding: The regional original places the upper Potengi southeast of Cerro Corá, with the selected opening approaching its southward bend and northeastward continuation. The opening is a chosen point, not a verified natural spring. Cunha et al. separately identify and map four Potengi springs in Serra de Santana; that small study footprint does not establish that the selected first point is any one of those springs.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Rio Potengi upper corridor, bounded cartographic identification

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Potengi through São Tomé
correspondence.finding: The labelled upper river runs northeast and east through the São Tomé setting, distinguished from the southern Riacho Cachoeirinha and the local Riacho Gameleira/other side drainage. The selected bends and continuation correspond at regional scale; small name-boundary or bank vertices are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Barcelona to São Paulo do Potengi
correspondence.finding: The eastward trunk continues by Barcelona before turning northeast toward São Paulo do Potengi. The mapped side branches near Lagoa de Velhos, Santa Rosa and Olho-d’Água remain separate. No nearby reservoir name is imposed on the selected river, and no detailed impoundment passage is claimed from this generalized sheet.

correspondence.component_scope: São Pedro and Ielmo Marinho continuation
correspondence.finding: The regional river is followed east past São Pedro and northeast to Ielmo Marinho. Riacho Salgado and Riacho da Velha are depicted as side drainage; downstream repeated Potengi labeling supports the selected receiving trunk rather than those tributaries.

correspondence.component_scope: São Gonçalo do Amarante and Natal estuary approach
correspondence.finding: The directly labelled Potengi continues through the São Gonçalo do Amarante setting into the broad waterway adjoining Natal. The southern Macaíba/Rio da Prata corridor is mapped separately. This establishes the receiving estuarine setting, without assigning every tidal channel or importing another tributary name.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final selected estuary-to-coast extension
correspondence.finding: The last selected path part projects generally eastward from the estuary toward the coast, while the regional original depicts the broad lower waterway turning north beside Natal before reaching the Atlantic. The available original does not establish a continuous water link along that chosen final extension. The discrepancy cannot be resolved by the shared Potengi label or general proximity to its mouth. Whether the selected extension crosses the urban strip is not established here; no exact coastline or bank test is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern opening and southwest-trending unnamed lake/stream feeder
correspondence.finding: The 76G original shows the chosen upper lake and the connected southwest-trending chain of narrow lakes and small streams. This chain rounds its western bend and joins the larger Western River corridor. The separate larger lake east of this opening and the farther-west river approach are not substituted for the selected feeder. The project map provides overlapping lake-chain orientation; the larger-scale 76G original supplies the actual small connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Western River join and southern lake bend
correspondence.finding: The named Western River approach from the west meets the selected feeder. The selection follows the eastern/southeastern receiving water, passes through elongated lake reaches to its southern turning lake, then takes the depicted northern/eastern lake outlet. The 76G original shows the lake arms and intervening links together; river-name lettering is not treated as a name for each lake.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Western River, with unnamed lake passages

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward connected lake and river sequence to the eastern turn
correspondence.finding: The route continues through the original map’s eastward sequence of irregular lake expansions and connecting channels. It passes the south sides of the main lake bodies and follows the eastern connection into the channel turning north. The lakes, outlet joins and the broader eastward bend are readable despite diagonal thematic overprinting. No separate names for these selected lakes were established.

correspondence.component_scope: Named northward Western River and overlapping map transition
correspondence.finding: Western River is directly printed beside the eastern northward corridor on 76G. The river turns northwest to the northern edge of that original and continues in the overlapping Sabina project map through the same confined valley, local widenings and successive joins. The inspected overlap establishes continuation rather than relying on shared basin membership.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Western River, Bathurst Lake separation and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The Sabina original depicts the selected lower river continuously northwest along the eastern side of the separate Bathurst Lake, with successive large meanders and its final outlet into the southern head of Bathurst Inlet. The selected route follows the river valley rather than traversing Bathurst Lake or the mapped winter ice road. Figure7.1-1 labels this same reach Kilokgiktok (Western River); its local-language spelling is recorded only as a source-specific label. CHS ARC403 chapter6 paragraph270 independently identifies Western River entering the head of Bathurst Inlet through a gorge. The terminal is supported at receiving-waterbody scale, not as a surveyed modern shoreline or tidal boundary.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Western River / southern head of Bathurst Inlet

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and upper Escatawpa corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected northern opening lies on the mapped Escatawpa River corridor east of State Line and northwest of Laton Hill. Repeated river labels and visible channels continue south through the Central Avenue crossing, past the Coaker Branch and Creeping Swamp Creek joins, and through the Fruitdale/Brushy Creek setting. The chosen opening is not asserted to be the ultimate or officially designated river source.

correspondence.component_scope: Vinegar Bend, Deer Park and Little Escatawpa junction
correspondence.finding: The labelled Escatawpa River follows the large bend through the Vinegar Bend setting and continues south past Deer Park. The map depicts the western Little Escatawpa River joining this trunk; the selected path remains on the Escatawpa corridor rather than following that separate tributary. The Okwake Creek joining setting and the connected passage across the county boundary are visible.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Alabama valley to the Mississippi crossing
correspondence.finding: The connected named river passes Bennett Creek, the Lotts Mill Creek and Pond Creek joining settings, Earlville and Franklin Creek, then Powell Creek, Brushy Creek and the Latonia/US98 crossing. The route continues southwest through the Red Creek joining setting into Mississippi. The named tributaries are orientation and junction evidence, not alternate names assigned to the trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Howell, Hurley and the lower river
correspondence.finding: The same named corridor continues through Howell Ferry/Waters Landing, across the George/Jackson county boundary and through the Wallace Creek, Page Creek and Spring Creek joining settings near Hurley. It crosses MS614, continues through the lower valley, and receives Big Creek and Lyons Creek near the Bird Lake/Lyons Lake surroundings. These nearby lake and floodplain features are preserved as local names; the selection does not require a separate reservoir or interbasin transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Escatawpa westward bend and Moss Point passage
correspondence.finding: The mapped river continues past Jackson Creek and Franklin Creek, crosses I10, turns west and passes the Black Creek joining setting. The broad connected lower watercourse reaches the Moss Point/East Moss Point urban setting. Beardslee Lake and O’Leary Lake are locally named widenings or adjoining water areas in this lower complex; their cartographic names are not overwritten by a scalar river name. Continuous mapped water connections establish the passage at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Escatawpa to Pascagoula confluence
correspondence.finding: Original cartography labels Escatawpa River through the Moss Point/Beardslee Lake setting. That broad watercourse joins the north-arriving Pascagoula corridor near Dog Island/Griffin Point and Sawmill Pointe. The selected route then turns south with the receiving Pascagoula River. This is a distinct downstream named component; the Escatawpa name is not extended over it.

correspondence.component_scope: Pascagoula downstream component and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected final corridor follows the mapped receiving Pascagoula River past the Lake Catch-em-all/Marsh Lake setting and the US90 crossing to the Pascagoula city waterfront. The actual modeled endpoint lies beside this lower river and industrial waterfront, north of its open Pascagoula Bay outlet. At the available generalized scale its last segment reaches the riverside/wharf edge rather than establishing an exact water-channel endpoint. Ordinary lower-river terminal-setting correspondence is supported; the endpoint is not relabelled as an offshore Gulf mouth, and no present navigable channel, bank position or tidal state is inferred.
